rationale: This is a sign-flipped repackaging of the archived "Current-Deficit Adjusted EBITDA Yield" (deficit moved from denominator to numerator) and it subtracts a balance-sheet stock from an annual flow, so for firms with large working-capital deficits the signal degenerates into a scaled negative leverage measure rather than an operating yield.

It is a predictable recombination of two archived legs (EBITDA yield × cash-runway denominator, cf. Loss-Runway OCF Yield), but substituting the cumulative retained deficit stock for the current-period loss flow is dimensionally coherent and a genuinely different notion of survival runway, so it is worth one test.

This bolts the archived weakest-link MIN operator onto the archive's best signal (Cash-Quality EBITDA Value) using a second leg that shares the same `che` numerator and is therefore highly collinear with the first, making it a cosmetic refinement rather than new economic content.

The `che/act` conditioner is now being applied mechanically to a fourth value denominator, and the dividend-yield leg has already failed twice in this archive (fmb 1.69 and 0.47) while also carrying a large zero-payer mass point that corrupts the rank transform.

The first leg is exactly 1 − che/act, so the construct is close to the algebraic complement of the archive's strongest signal, and because the value leg itself loads positively the product's natural direction is ambiguous — the stated negative expected sign is not what the expression reliably delivers.

Heavily templated on existing revt/mcap × liquidity combinations, but it directly tests the archive's central tension — cash-based conditioners produced positive FF5 alphas while every sales-to-price variant produced strong FMB slopes with zero or negative alpha — so the outcome is diagnostically informative rather than merely another variant.
